parsed.why: No trans-specific offence, facilities or document exposure. But documented anti-LGBT violence, dismissive police refusing to investigate, slurs against gender-nonconforming men, evangelical hostility to gay tourists; no protections, trans data silent.

Legal same-sex conduct since 1977, hate-crime law covering gender identity, minority protections, travel guide acceptance. Offset by unevenly enforced discrimination law, inadequate hate-crime investigations, rural hostility and escalating anti-gender politics.

Police documented as main source of violence against trans people — rape, beatings, victims reframed as perpetrators with impunity; sodomy still criminalised with sporadic arrests. Third-gender tradition and sanctuary village mitigate, but no recourse exists.

State-imposed universal exposure: passports/visas that cannot match, entry refusal and lifetime-ineligibility risk, facility bans in ~21 states, birth-sex custody with documented abuse. National protections and courts only partly offset.

Decriminalised 2025; domestic-violence act expressly covers gender identity and gives trans victims remedies; police, ports and customs trained. But violence against visiting gay men, asylum finding of persecution risk, UN declaration opposition; no trans data.
